Characterizing components of energy balance - including appetite and dietary intake regulation -
is important for optimizing behavioral interventions to mitigate obesity and chronic disease
burden. This study is the first to assess laboratory-based appetite and dietary intake – and the
impact of an acute bout of REx on these parameters – in any population of cancer survivors.
Although our study found differences in appetite hormones in the hours after REx that should
result in decreased hunger and increased satiety among BCS, this was not reflected in
subjective appetite perceptions or energy intake. Fat-free mass and RMR were related to
